Bitcoin stabilized near $60,800 on the morning of June 25, clawing back from an overnight dip below $59,000. Market sentiment remains severely depressed, with the Fear & Greed Index plummeting to an abysmal 12 out of 100. Institutional hemorrhage accelerated yesterday as U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs bled a staggering $469 million in a fifth consecutive day of outflows. Yet amidst this capitulation, spot XRP ETFs uniquely defied the trend, registering $2.05 million in net inflows as allocators hunt for alternative regulatory catalysts ahead of the EU's July 1 MiCA deadline.

This intense crypto pessimism sharply contrasts with surging traditional equities. Driven by a massive Micron Technology earnings beat, Nasdaq 100 futures rallied 1.8% this morning. With Brent crude plunging to $72 a barrel on U.S.-Iran shipping resolutions, the 10-year Treasury yield held at 4.41% as global liquidity braces for today's pivotal U.S. PCE inflation release.
